interactions.summary: A student asks whether defining God as love imposes motives or behavioral constraints on God, and Jiang answers that it means God is perfect and loves unconditionally.

A student asks why Protestantism preserved the Holy Spirit and the Trinity if Dante is the hidden source, and Jiang answers that Protestantism is mainly a political rebellion against Catholic authority whose key theological move is direct access to God through the Bible rather than ecclesial mediation.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student question, Jiang answer, student clarification, Jiang reply

interactions.summary: One student proposes that Dante opens love as another channel to God beyond the Bible, and an online comment begins pushing the problem of whether a God who is the source of everything must also contain hate.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student hypothesis and moderator relay of online comment

claims.claim: Jiang says that if God is love, then God is perfect, loves unconditionally, and cannot be angered into hatred.
He argues that Protestantism is not primarily an attempt to promote Dante but a rebellion of local princes against the authority of the Catholic Church.
Jiang says the doctrine of the Trinity is politically useful because mystery trains obedience to authority.
He says Protestant influence from Dante would have been indirect and largely unconscious rather than a self-aware adoption of Dante's theology.
Jiang frames the core Protestant idea as direct connection to God through the Bible, against a Church that insists believers must come through priestly mediation.

signature_moments.moment: The Trinity is described less as a truth claim than as a machine for obedience because mystery forces submission to authority.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it creates obedience to authority because because of mystery
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This gives Jiang a concrete political use for theological unintelligibility and links the lecture's anti-mystery argument to church power.

signature_moments.moment: Protestantism is compressed into one decisive inversion: you can go to God through the Bible without the Church standing in the middle.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you have a direct connection to god for the bible
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It sharpens Jiang's contrast between mediated Catholic authority and a more direct, text-enabled relation to God.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang treats it as a geopolitical rebellion against Catholic authority whose central religious promise is more direct access to God and scripture.
Jiang's shorthand for the Protestant claim that a believer can approach God through scripture without the Church acting as the necessary gatekeeper.

uncertainty_notes.note: The final student hypothesis and online comment are interrupted before Jiang answers, so this packet should preserve them as setup pressure rather than a completed doctrine.
